thread:
incident-bot: PAGER -> maya: P1 - CYPRESSLABS (prod, private VPC, dedicated pool) reporting mass auth failures (401) from tenant 'cypress-main' starting ~09:12 UTC. Pager: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): i'll take this. thanks bot. paging liam + raj. any immediate customer impact numbers?

cypress-ms-ops (customer): we started seeing errors around 09:10. tokens validated fine on our side; many requests into your endpoint getting 401. impacting api and webhooks.

liam (sre): looking at auth-bridge logs (vpc-auth-proxy) - a lot of jwks fetch failures, then introspect returning 401. sample log: `GET /.well-known/jwks.json -> error x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid`.

raj (infra): confirmed: egress call to customer IdP JWKS is failing TLS handshake from our auth nodes. error shows our client cert chain rejected by their TLS layer after our keystore rotation at 02:00 UTC.

maya (oncall): can you paste the exact error blob?

liam (sre): ```
2026-03-15T09:13:22Z auth-proxy vpc-3a: jwks-fetch failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
x509: certificate has expired
stack: net/http.(*Client).Do ...
```

cypress-ms-ops (customer): we did rotate our signing key earlier today (we removed old KID). we _did not_ expect you to rotate the client cert bundle; are you saying your client cert expired?

raj (infra): our keystore rotation pushed a new client cert chain to vpc-auth nodes. looks like the new chain isn't trusted by the customer's IdP (maybe missing intermediate or different EKU). we need to avoid failing auth path.

amelia (acct mgmt): i'm on it from the customer comms side. i'll update Cypress leadership and coordination channel. they want ETA and a temporary fallback.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable tenant-level jwks-cache fallback to hosted jwks proxy for cypress-main (pulls from cache / mirrors) 2) route auth calls for that tenant to hosted-auth-proxy (no mTLS) as a short-lived bypass while infra assesses cert chain. performing change now.

maya (oncall): command to enable fallback: `redwood auth route update --tenant cypress-main --auth-proxy hosted-auth-proxy --jwks-fallback hosted-cache --ttl 600`

deploy-bot: route update applied by maya at 2026-03-15T09:18:55Z - /customers/cypress-main now routed to hosted-auth-proxy (temp) :white_check_mark:

liam (sre): after routing change, 401 rate dropped from ~45% -> ~0.7% within 90s. looks good. watching for any regressions.

raj (infra): root cause: our rotated client cert chain lacks intermediate CA that customer's IdP requires. remediation options: A) re-deploy previous client cert chain to vpc-auth-proxies (quick rollback) B) coordinate with customer to accept new chain (longer) C) keep hosted fallback until a combined maintenance window. planning rollback now as quick fix.

cypress-ms-ops (customer): we'll accept a short maintenance window to update our IdP trust store, but want minimum downtime. please do the quick rollback and then we'll test.

maya (oncall): rolling back keystore on vpc-auth nodes to previous chain. executing controlled restart of auth-proxy pods in batches of 2. ETA ~35m. posting exact steps in runbook.

liam (sre): monitoring metrics: token introspect latency normal. no sign of increased error budget.

amelia (acct mgmt): sending external update to Cypress: "we implemented a temporary auth routing fallback, errors reduced significantly, we will perform a controlled rollback of our client cert chain in ~35m and coordinate a maintenance window for final fix." :mailbox_with_mail:

maya (oncall): handoff note for night oncall (nora): - incident P1 reduced to P0.3 after fallback. - current state: tenant routed to hosted-auth-proxy; rollback in progress (batches). - customer agreed to maintenance to accept new chain later. - runbook link: https://confluence.internal/incidents/cypress-auth-2276543210 (contains commands + verification).

nora (oncall-next): acknowledged, i'll pick up in 40m. please paste the quick validation checklist here before handoff.

maya (oncall): validation checklist: 1) confirm `curl -v https://auth-proxy.internal/introspect` returns 200 for sample jwt 2) check Prometheus: `sum(rate(auth_introspect_errors_total[1m]))` for tenant label <= 1 3) verify jwks fetch success logs contain `200 OK` 4) customer confirm end-to-end auth flow via their staging callback. rollback rollback-cmd: `redwood infra keystore rollback --pool vpc-auth-3a --to-tag v2026-03-14-previous`

cypress-ms-ops (customer): thanks, will coordinate test on our side and report back.

liam (sre): leaving a note in postmortem draft: cause = keystore rotation produced cert chain incompatible with customer IdP; mitigations = tenant-level jwks fallback + route to hosted-auth-proxy; long-term fix = stricter preflight validation of cert chains + allowlist test against customer IdP prior to rollouts.

maya (oncall): closing active page because customer-facing impact mitigated by fallback and rollback in progress. if anything spikes, re-open P1. :thumbsup:
